title: Efficiency across the model lifecycle
introduction: My guiding belief is that a useful model can succeed without leading every benchmark, but a business built around it needs sustainable costs. I focus on accelerating pre-training, post-training, and inference without sacrificing model performance, so that the same capability becomes cheaper to build and use.

areas.label: 01 / PRE-TRAINING
areas.title: Train efficiently
areas.description: Distributed training, communication efficiency, and runtime performance analysis to make better use of available compute.

areas.label: 02 / POST-TRAINING
areas.title: Adapt efficiently
areas.description: Memory-efficient fine-tuning and agentic learning, including low-rank adaptation and post-training for long-horizon coding agents.

areas.label: 03 / INFERENCE
areas.title: Serve efficiently
areas.description: Quantization and efficient execution for large language models, mixture-of-experts models, and multi-model agents.

approach.label: Research approach
approach.title: Algorithm–system co-design
approach.description: I study learning algorithms together with the systems that execute them: numerical representations, memory use, communication, and hardware behavior. The aim is faster execution and lower cost at the same level of model performance.

evidence.title: Why cost matters
evidence.subtitle: The economics of staying in business · 2024–2026
evidence.overview: Businesses need models that meet their quality requirements at a cost they can sustain. At high request volumes, even a small per-token price difference changes the monthly bill. My goal is to reduce that bill by accelerating the full model lifecycle while preserving model performance.

charts.title: Serving efficiency becomes cheaper access
charts.takeaway: GPT-5.6 Luna received an 80% API price cut after improvements to model-serving efficiency.
charts.highlight_label: API prices for the same named model
charts.note: Announced rates after the cut: $0.20 input / $1.20 output per 1M tokens. OpenAI attributes the change to efficiency improvements across models, inference systems, and context management.

charts.title: A lower price expands the budget
charts.takeaway: Haiku 5.5 lowered input and output token prices by 90% for prompts up to 100k tokens.
charts.note: Standard input / output prices per 1M tokens: Haiku 4.5 $1.00 / $5.00; Haiku 5.5 $0.10 / $0.50. Haiku 5.5 also reported higher benchmark scores than its predecessor.
charts.highlight_label: Input and output prices · prompts ≤100k tokens

limitations.title: Scope of the comparison
limitations.description: Monthly bills are illustrative calculations at a fixed token volume, not measured production spending or a claim of equal capability. Rates exclude caching, batch discounts, and other business costs. Haiku 5.5 prices shown apply to prompts up to 100k tokens. The 2025 benchmarks used different thinking budgets. The closure cases do not measure survival probabilities or isolate price as the cause; OctoAI’s closure followed an acquisition.

evidence.date_note: Evidence window · 2024–2026. Sources checked October 8, 2026. Prices are USD at the stated announcement dates.

operating_costs.title: What it costs to keep serving users
operating_costs.takeaway: The same request volume can produce very different inference bills. Lower spending leaves more revenue to cover people, infrastructure, and continued operations.

performance_context.title: Performance is a requirement; cost is a business constraint
performance_context.description: Haiku 4.5 remained a lower-priced API option despite scoring below the frontier Sonnet 4.5 on the 2025 SWE-bench Verified report (73.3% vs. 77.2%). This supports choosing sufficient capability for a workload rather than paying for benchmark leadership on every request.
